---
title: "Exercise · Understand a Pico"
---

A short, guided inspection of the two files the Pico course already
ships. Complete it before moving on to the lab.

See the [Open Engineering Language Server (OELS) onboarding guide](../../../../oels.qmd)
for the local install and editor setup.

{{< include ../../../../shared/includes/oels.qmd >}}


## Task

Read the two files below and answer three questions.

1. Open [`definitions/pico.yaml`](../../../../definitions/pico.yaml) —
   the OE Pico artefact contract this repository ships.
2. Open the Hello Pico reference Rule in
   [`labs/hello-pico/solution.qmd`](../../../../labs/hello-pico/solution.html)
   (the `rules/hello.yaml` block).

Answer:

- **Q1.** Which fields does `definitions/pico.yaml` list as **required**
  on an OE-shaped Pico (`spec.target.kind: Pico`)?
- **Q2.** Which keys does the Hello Pico Rule use, and are those keys
  the same as the required Pico fields?
- **Q3.** For each anatomy item from
  [`memo24.md`](../../../../memo24.md) §2.3 — **Face**, **Muscles**,
  **Memory**, **Hands**, **Nervous System**, **Rules**, **Discovery**,
  **Operations** — is it **required by schema** on every Pico, or is
  it **optional** today?

## Success criteria

- [ ] You can name every required field in `definitions/pico.yaml`.
- [ ] You can state the three keys of the Hello Pico Rule and how they
      differ from the Pico shape.
- [ ] You classify each of the eight anatomy items as required or
      optional and can point at `definitions/pico.yaml` to justify
      each answer.

## Automatable check

Keep this check — it is unchanged from the previous version of this
exercise and demonstrates the current `pico parse` step runs
end-to-end. From a scratch working directory, with the
[Hello Pico one-time setup](../../../../labs/hello-pico/objectives.html#one-time-setup)
applied so `pico` resolves to this repository's `bin/pico`:

```bash
cat > /tmp/hello.yaml <<'YAML'
id: rule.hello
kind: greeting
value: "Hello, Pico!"
YAML
pico parse /tmp/hello.yaml --out /tmp/parsed.json \
  && echo "OK: parsed /tmp/hello.yaml"
```

The command exits with status `0` and prints an `OK:` line when the
Rule matches the three-key shape the reference Parser accepts
([`bin/pico`](../../../../bin/pico) lines 56 and 82–86).

## Worked answer

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show worked answer"}

**Q1 — Required fields in `definitions/pico.yaml`.**
The target schema (`spec.target.kind: Pico`) requires:

```
apiVersion
kind
metadata.name
spec.type
spec.capabilities
spec.implementation
spec.state
spec.events
```

No other top-level field is required; `spec.additionalProperties: true`
means a Pico may carry extra sibling fields, but none of them is
required by name.

**Q2 — Keys in the Hello Pico Rule.**
`rules/hello.yaml` uses three keys only: `id`, `kind`, `value`. These
are the keys of a **Rule**, not of a Pico — the Hello Pico Rule is
input to `pico parse` → `pico compose`, which emits a shell-script
artefact. The required Pico fields above (`apiVersion`, `spec.type`,
`spec.capabilities`, etc.) are a different, OE-shaped Pico resource
contract. The Hello Pico lab exercises the Rules → Parser → Composer
pipeline; it does not author an OE-shaped Pico resource against
`definitions/pico.yaml`.

**Q3 — Anatomy items: required by schema, or optional?**

| Anatomy item (memo24 §2.3)      | Required by `definitions/pico.yaml`? | Why                                                                                   |
|---------------------------------|---------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Face (Python)                   | Optional                              | Not named in the schema's `required` list.                                            |
| Muscles (Rust+PyO3)             | Optional                              | Not named in the schema's `required` list.                                            |
| Memory (Celld)                  | Optional                              | Not named in the schema's `required` list.                                            |
| Hands (Composio)                | Optional                              | Not named in the schema's `required` list.                                            |
| Nervous System (EMQX)           | Optional                              | Not named in the schema's `required` list.                                            |
| Rules (OE Rules)                | Optional                              | Not named in the schema's `required` list.                                            |
| Discovery (A2A)                 | Optional                              | Not named in the schema's `required` list.                                            |
| Operations (OE Operations)      | Optional                              | Not named in the schema's `required` list.                                            |

Every anatomy item is a *capability* a Pico may compose through
`spec.capabilities`; none is named as a required field in the schema.
A minimal Pico that declares `spec.capabilities: []` is still valid
against `definitions/pico.yaml`.
:::
